quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 22

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads, what happens to your tires?

options.text: Your tires grip better than on pavement.
Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
You can see the road better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Tires grip loose gravel and dirt roads less than hard pavement. You must slow down. It takes longer to stop and you can skid more easily when turning.

questions.question: What does alcohol affect first?

options.text: Vision.
Judgment.
Balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the part of your brain that controls judgment and skill. This happens before it affects other abilities you need to drive safely.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaching, what must you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.
questions.explanation: Pull to the right edge of the road and stop when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights. On one-way streets, move toward the nearest edge of the road.

questions.question: Before starting the car, you should:

options.text: Buckle your safety belt.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.
Do both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both of the above.
questions.explanation: Before you start the car, buckle your safety belt and make sure all passengers buckle theirs too.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Slow down and use your low beam headlights in fog. If you cannot see the road, pull over and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: When parallel parking while facing downhill, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn them sharply toward the side of the road.
Turn them away from the side of the road.
Keep them straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them sharply toward the side of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb. When parking uphill without a curb, turn them toward the edge. When parking uphill with a curb, turn them away from the curb.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign shows a pedestrian crossing. Be alert and let pedestrians cross safely.

questions.question: Which statement about large trucks is true?

options.text: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
They all have air brakes that let them stop quickly.
They are easier to turn than passenger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need almost twice as much distance to stop. At 55 mph, a passenger car stops in about 400 feet, but a large truck needs almost 800 feet.

questions.question: When must you obey school crossing guards?

options.text: At all times.
Only during school hours.
Only if you see children present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Always obey school crossing guards when near a school.

questions.question: What speed should you always travel at?

options.text: The speed of other vehicles around you.
The speed limit.
A speed that fits the road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: A speed that fits the road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Drive at a speed that matches the road conditions, weather, and legal speed limit. Never drive above the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: A bad suspension can cause:

options.text: Vehicle control problems.
Squealing brakes.
Loose steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicle control problems.
questions.explanation: Your suspension helps you control your vehicle and gives a smooth ride. If your car bounces a lot after hitting a bump or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: When a school bus stops to load or unload children, you must:

options.text: Stop completely until all children leave the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes up.
Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes up.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and a stop arm extended, you must stop completely. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes up. Even after the bus moves, do not go until you know no children are crossing in front of you.

questions.question: As you drive faster, it is important to:

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look far ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle needs more distance to stop as you go faster. When driving at high speeds, look far ahead so you have time to safely react to hazards.

questions.question: Before entering a curve:

options.text: Use your turn signal.
Slow down.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: You can drive slower than the speed limit for safety reasons. Slow down for curves, hills with limited visibility, slippery roads, and areas with animals or pedestrians.

questions.question: When driving at night, when should you use high beam headlights?

options.text: When an oncoming vehicle is less than one block away.
When you are following another vehicle in heavy traffic.
When no oncoming vehicles are near.

questions.correctAnswerText: When no oncoming vehicles are near.
questions.explanation: Use high beams on dark roads to see ahead. Switch to low beams at least 500 feet before meeting oncoming vehicles. Also use low beams when following another vehicle within 300 feet.

questions.question: Use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days:

options.text: To keep your engine warm.
So other drivers can see your vehicle.
To warn others about the bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: So other drivers can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: In rain, snow, or fog, other drivers have trouble seeing your vehicle. Headlights make your vehicle more visible. If you need to use windshield wipers, turn on your low beam headlights.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:

options.text: Right turn.
Intersection.
Lane change.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that your road ends at an intersection ahead. Slow down and be ready to yield or stop before turning.

questions.question: When driving in fog or mist, do not use high beam headlights because:

options.text: The light reflects back into your eyes.
Oncoming vehicles might not see you.
Vehicles behind you may drive too close.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light reflects back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, do not use high beams because the light bounces back into your eyes.

questions.question: To pass on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check the distance to oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the distance to oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are going. They may be faster than they look. Always make sure you have enough space to pass safely. If you are unsure of an oncoming vehicle's speed, wait to pass until it has passed and you have clear space.

questions.question: If you face a green light but traffic blocks the intersection ahead, you should:

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Stay out of the intersection until traffic moves.
Follow other vehicles and enter the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until traffic moves.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter the intersection if traffic blocks your way. If you get stuck in the intersection when the light turns red, you block other traffic. You can get a ticket for blocking an intersection.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line between two lanes mean?

options.text: Both lanes are going in the same direction.
You can pass when it is safe.
You cannot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line separates lanes going in opposite directions. You can pass if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is stopped ahead with its lights on. What should you do?

options.text: Ask the emergency workers if they need help.
Speed up to get around the scene quickly.
Move to the farthest lane away from the vehicle or slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the farthest lane away from the vehicle or slow down.
questions.explanation: Move to a lane away from the emergency vehicle if possible. If you cannot move over, slow down to a safe speed and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When must you use your low beams?

options.text: On a lighted street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off precipitation and create glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: You should not enter an intersection if the light will turn red before you clear it. When does this rule apply?

options.text: Under any circumstances.
Unless you entered on a yellow light.
Unless you entered on a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under any circumstances.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter an intersection unless you can get completely across before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: On a highway, you see a single broken white line. What can you do?

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You can cross to pass or change lanes.
You can only cross to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can cross to pass or change lanes.
questions.explanation: A broken white line separates lanes going the same direction. You can cross it to pass or change lanes if it is safe.
